milestone.name: PCBE-1 extends bounded certificate to flags, arithmetic and dependency identities

tests.same_source_changed_flag: FAIL as required with derived 7 versus claimed 42
tests.dependency_digest_mismatch: FAIL as required with selected mismatch branch

milestone.complexity: For acyclic tree-form PCBE-1 expressions, proof has one record per checked AST node and checker work is structural/linear in checked nodes plus compared digest-string length.
milestone.revision: The zero-executor certificate must distinguish declared/readable premises from opaque ambient facts. PCBE-1 can derive a deterministic result conditional on declared environment/configuration and dependency identities, but it cannot discover the actual CPU/toolchain/filesystem/network state without measurement. This prevents a false upgrade from proof-about-premises to proof-about-the-world.

certifying_compilers.finding: A certifying compiler produces both object code and a certificate; independent verification can distrust the compiler, but fresh code+certificate production still needs compilation.

necula_certifying_compiler.finding: The compiler/certifier ensemble can generate a formal proof or counterexample, reinforcing that result verification can be simpler than compiler verification but does not eliminate fresh compilation.

foundational_pcc.finding: FPCC emphasizes a very small/simple proof checker and minimized trusted base, supporting the small-checker asymmetry sought here; production of certified code remains a separate process.

compcert.finding: CompCert gives a proved semantic-preservation theorem for code it produces, but a fresh executable still comes from running the compiler; formal compiler verification is not itself a zero-executor build result.

literature_audit.phase1_conclusion: These mechanisms strengthen verification/trust separation, but none is a general accepted Phase-1 route when fresh certificate or target generation requires an external compiler/prover. PCBE-1 is acceptable only because scheduled Chat itself derives the finite certificate in the tested tiny semantics.

pcbe1.scope: declared finite premises and small acyclic expression grammar

actual_ambient_environment_claim.reason: certificate verification does not measure the physical environment

negative_evidence: A small proof checker does not imply a zero-executor fresh proof producer.
A verified compiler does not imply a compiler-free fresh artifact.
A certificate conditional on ENV(MODE)=1 cannot certify that an opaque machine actually has MODE=1 unless that premise comes from an independently trusted/readable source.
PCBE-1's O(n) checker claim is structural for its tiny tree grammar, not a performance benchmark or claim about realistic compilation.

frontier.action: Add premise-origin tags to PCBE: REPO_IDENTITY, DECLARED_CONFIG, DERIVED and EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION. Acceptance checker must reject EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION unless an independently valid certificate is attached. Test that repository Git blob identity from r145 can be reused as a dependency premise without binary byte readback or rebuilding.

Build a reuse-only capsule combining r145 content-addressed Git identity with PCBE-1: declared release flag plus exact expected blob SHA gates an artifact-selection/result claim; mutate flag and SHA separately and require rejection.

Search proof-producing compilation for certificate formats where generation could itself be expressed in bounded declarative rules. Reject general systems that require compiler/theorem-prover execution; preserve only smaller finite subsets as candidate grammars.

exact_next_action: Define PCBE premise-origin policy: REPO_IDENTITY may be accepted only when the connector exposes an exact Git blob SHA at a bound path; DECLARED_CONFIG is a conditional premise, never a claim about ambient reality; EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION is rejected without a separate valid certificate. Using the r145 payload blob identity already in own state, construct a reuse-only rule that returns RELEASE_OK iff MODE==1 and payload SHA equals the expected blob. Recheck one positive, one changed-MODE negative and one changed-SHA negative without reading binary bytes or rebuilding. Persist whether identity-only artifact reuse closes any richer-mode dependency beyond r145's existing transaction capsule.
termination: intermediate Phase-1 checkpoint with nonempty frontier; global completion false; recurring role remains enabled
